The entire submitted chapter is correct under the stipulated accepted prerequisites and standard inputs. The affine quotient is well-defined for arbitrary smooth real nonclosed theta. The elementary smooth/current HBC(1,1) identification supplies smooth representatives, and their derivatives characterize exactly the specified fiber. Proper degree-one pushforward works because the background and its derivative are pulled from the fixed base. Distributional ddc commutes with pushforward; elliptic regularity makes the difference potential between smooth representatives smooth, establishing pullback independence and push-pull identity. Positivity, metric-independent affine nefness and the Cartier definition are used consistently. BGL25 Definition 1.1 and Lemma 1.4 match the terminology; its different ddc normalization leaves the quotient image unchanged. [Publisher text](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42543-025-00105-2).

The accepted compatible divisorial currents and original-background majorant prove pseudoeffectivity and compatibility. Multiplier-ideal equivalence and smooth ddc gauge changes preserve the family. For arbitrary genuine qpsh u, a local smooth psh correction preserves multiplier ideals and pulled-back Lelong numbers. The Bergman bound gives the upper divisorial inequality; Jacobian change of variables gives a+A_E>m nu_E and hence the lower inequality. These use precisely the manuscript's squared-logarithm and exponential-weight normalization. Passing to the integer limit identifies self-trace with the full summable Siu divisor on every model, and nonclosed divisorial removal gives the positive residual representative.

The rational-coefficient, bounded-remainder analytic convention yields a finite effective rational divisor after log resolution. Divisor metrics give a globally bounded residual potential v and smooth beta with d beta=pi*d theta. Demailly regularization applies to the closed current ddc v with the arbitrary smooth lower bound -beta. Unit ideals make the actual Bergman/cutoff construction smooth, giving almost-positive representatives in the same fixed affine class. This smoothness is verified from Theorem 14.12's construction and observation 14.14 in the supplied July 2011 source. Further modifications preserve boundedness of the residual potential and introduce exactly the pullback divisor, proving the nef Cartier realization. The nearby Kähler-only nef lemma in SGPT is not used for this extension.

For arbitrary singularities, exact analytic type (1/m,I(mu)) gives the stated D_m,Z on each fixed model. Adding 2 epsilon_m omega supplies the required positive background theta_m. Strong linear trace-mass convergence gives the asserted weak convergence of C_m,Z, and closedness of D_m,Z gives exactly dC_m,Z=pi*d theta+2 epsilon_m pi*d omega, with smooth convergence. The backgrounds and their derivatives may vary. No unrestricted weak quotient continuity, fixed-derivative approximation, closed nef approximation or nonlinear volume continuity is inferred. All type and dimension conditions, including n=1, are consistent.

The accepted infinite-mass witness has unit multiplier ideals at every positive weight. Their orders vanish on every modification, and the self-trace identity forces every divisorial coefficient to vanish, including exceptional ones. Its affine family therefore equals that of zero and has the nef Cartier realization (Y,{omega}), while its raw extended mass is infinite and the smooth mass is finite. No BMP/PVP assumption or novelty claim is used.
